description_full: Carpenter Technology Corporation manufactures, fabricates, and distributes specialty metals in the United States, Europe, the Asia Pacific, Mexico, Canada, and internationally. It operates in two segments, Specialty Alloys Operations and Performance Engineered Products. The company offers specialty alloys, including titanium alloys, powder metals, stainless steels, alloy steels, and tool steels, as well as metal powders and parts. It serves the aerospace, defense, medical, transportation, energy, industrial, and consumer markets. The company was founded in 1889 and is headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

financial_summary: Carpenter Technology Corporatio is a large-cap industrials business with a $13.8B market cap on $3.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 14% against a 10% cost of capital, a 3-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 17% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $362M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.14× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.4× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 19× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.6%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 2.5% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
